source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide why some exposed foods rot while pickles and murabbas with enough salt or sugar do not get infected in the same way.
node_labels: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Even a tiny amount of salt or sugar prevents microorganisms from infecting food.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Food rots first, and the rotting produces microorganisms.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Food exposed only to air cannot rot, because microorganisms occur only in water and soil.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: A pickle cannot get infected, even without enough salt or sugar, because it is a pickle.

intelligence.enrichment: Microorganisms can be found everywhere, including water, soil, air, surfaces, and some food items. Spices with high concentrations of salt or sugar act as preservatives because they do not allow these organisms to infect pickles and murabbas. Microbes present in surroundings -> exposed food can rot; high salt or sugar preservative conditions -> microbial infection is prevented. The learner correctly applies this rule: Microorganisms can be found everywhere, including water, soil, air, surfaces, and some food items. Spices with high concentrations of salt or sugar act as preservatives because they do not allow these organisms to infect pickles and murabbas. Pickles stay safe because they are pickles, while fresh foods rot because they are naturally weak.
